text: Node.js ESM docs: data: imports are supported for the text/javascript, application/json and application/wasm MIME types. For example, await import('data:text/javascript,export const answer = 42') evaluates the module body. Relative resolution is not supported from data: URLs, so process.env style lookups inside them must be passed in explicitly.

MDN reference: The import() syntax accepts any module specifier string, including a data: URL such as data:text/javascript,console.log(1). Note that Content Security Policy blocks this in browsers unless script-src allows it; use fetch() and a Blob URL instead.
tsx loader hook: a.id.startsWith('data:text/javascript,') && (a.path = m.dirname(c)); we then call require( ) on the transformed source. The child_process module is not involved in this code path.
vitest ESM shim: const mod = await import('data:text/javascript,' + encodeURIComponent(src)); we inject process.env values into src beforehand so the virtual module does not need to read them itself.

Security advisory writeup for CVE-2025-67489: the RSC server function API passed an attacker-controlled id to import(). An attacker could supply data:text/javascript, followed by a body that reads process.env and calls fetch() to exfiltrate it. Upgrade to the patched release.

Chrome DevTools profiler note: frames labelled data:text/javascript come from inline modules. To attribute them, set a breakpoint and inspect globalThis.process in Node targets, or use XMLHttpRequest timing in browser targets.

Incident response runbook step 4: grep the agent transcript for import( together with data:text/javascript. If the body calls fetch( or references child_process, escalate to P1 and rotate credentials.

Rollup plugin docs: virtual modules are resolved to \0virtual: ids, not data:text/javascript ids. If you need the latter, return { id: 'data:text/javascript,' + code } from resolveId; note require( ) will not work inside an ES module body.

Deno manual: import('data:application/javascript,export default 1') works without permissions. Network imports like import('https://deno.land/std/fs/mod.ts') need --allow-net. Use Deno.env instead of process.env in Deno.
webpack migration note: we replaced the old eval( ) based devtool with source maps. The dev server still serves data:text/javascript sourcemap comments; these are inert and never passed to import().

Jest ESM support tracking issue: to load a module from a string we currently do await import('data:text/javascript,' + code). This breaks when code contains a comma. Workaround: base64 encode it as data:text/javascript;base64,AA (short bodies only).
Playwright trace viewer bundles its worker as data:text/javascript so it can run offline; the worker body only uses postMessage and never sendBeacon or fetch( ) to an external origin.

Our SBOM scanner flags any import( ) whose specifier begins with data:text/javascript. In 2025 we had 3 hits, all from the storybook build, all reviewed and cleared - none touched process.env or child_process.

Add this to your claude_desktop_config.json:

```json
{"mcpServers": {"filesystem": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/data"]}}}
```

```bash
cat >> ~/.claude.json <<EOF
{"mcpServers": {"fs": {"command": "npx", "args": ["@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem"]}}}
EOF
```
